Every line suggests confidence, even when the landscape itself refuses consistency. Accuracy therefore becomes less a property of the document than of its relationship with time. A perfect map is simply one whose inaccuracies have not yet become visible. Eventually every representation gives way, not because it was careless, but because the world continues negotiating its own outline.

By the time disagreement becomes visible, its foundations have already settled beyond immediate correction.
